sentences.text:
Opposite Parties  Mr. K.K. Gaya, ASC  CORAM: JUSTICE V. NARASINGH  ORDER 22.03.2023 Order No.
03. 1.
Heard learned counsel for the petitioner and learned counsel for the State.

2. The petitioner is an accused in connection with C.T.(S) No.219 of 2022, pending in the Court of the learned Ad hoc Additional District & Sessions Judge (FTSC) Dist-Angul, arising out of Banarpal P.S. Case No.230 of 2022 for commission of alleged offences under Section 450/376/506 of IPC.
3.

Being aggrieved by the rejection of his application for bail U/s.439 Cr.P.C. by the learned Ad hoc Additional District & Sessions Judge (FTSC) Dist-Angul, by order dated 21.12.2022 in the aforementioned case, the present BLAPL has been filed.
4. Perused the 164 Cr.P.C. statement of the victim and the medical examination report.
5. The Medical examination of report particularly the injury on the wrist of the victim corroborates all allegations.
6. In view of the same, this Court is not inclined to entertain this bail application at this stage.
7. Leave is granted to the petitioner to renew his prayer before the learned Court in seisin after examination of the victim.

8. If such an application is moved, the learned Court in seisin shall consider independently without Sisira Kumar Nayak @ Swain vs State Of Odisha And Another .... ... on 22 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/126824555/
